title: Sync-health monitor for large WooCommerce catalogs
subtitle: Follow-up run testing the pivot from the earlier throttled-sync report: a plugin that watches whichever Meta/Google sync plugin a store already uses and alerts on failures.

follows.title: Throttled catalog sync for large WooCommerce stores

verdict.summary: The pain holds up. Different store owners, across four sync plugins and three sites, describe jobs that stall for days while dashboards say there are no errors (e1, e7, e10). But the monitor as pitched doesn't clear GO. Nobody visibly pays for monitoring on its own: the closest WP.org twin, CatalogCanary, has fewer than 10 installs, and a Shopify monitor has 0 reviews. Feed vendors already email on failed runs. Google pushes approval changes for free. Reading Meta-side status needs App Review. The pivot left to test is an agency multi-site watchdog that reads local jobs only, pre-sold before any build.

opportunities.name: Sync-health monitor alongside existing sync plugins
opportunities.one_liner: Alerts when Meta/Google/feed plugin jobs fail, products silently stop syncing, or get disapproved. Freemium, $79-149/yr.
opportunities.why: Pain 7: two high themes from different authors on WP.org, wpde.org and the Merchant Center community, mostly from 2026 (e1-e12, e20). Not 8, because posters noticed and asked for help, and few say they left. WTP 4: stores pay for Pro feed plugins (e22-e26), a substitute, but there's no evidence anyone pays for monitoring alone (e43, e52). Gap 4: Google covers big drops for free (e28) and pushes approval changes through its API (e55); WP Product Feed Manager and RexTheme already email on failed runs (e53, e38); CatalogCanary ships a stuck-run watchdog (e50); six other 2026 entrants do local audits (e34, e36, e37). A cross-plugin job monitor wasn't found. Fit 6: local job watching is core Woo work, but Meta status needs App Review (e57). Reach 6: the WooCommerce Facebook group (e46), Woo Slack (e47), wpde.org (e9) and the GMC community (e20) exist, but only WP.org shows volume, and it bans promotion (e48). Build 5: a local MVP takes weeks, but platform reads need OAuth verification (e58) and a hosted endpoint.

gap.statement: WooCommerce stores with thousands of products that already run a sync or feed plugin can't tell when sync quietly stops, because the plugin dashboards and job logs report "no errors" while products stay unsynced or feeds go stale, and the free platform alerts only fire on large Google-side drops.

pains.theme: Sync looks healthy while nothing syncs
pains.summary: The dashboard says no errors or setup is complete, and jobs show as completed, but products stay unsynced or at 0.

pains.theme: Jobs stall or stop quietly for days
pains.summary: Feeds stuck at a percentage, frozen Action Scheduler queues, and stale last-updated dates.

pains.theme: Products go missing or are rejected in bulk
pains.summary: Whole categories or catalogs drop out of feeds or get rejected, often found late.

competitors.name: Google Merchant Center + Merchant API
competitors.positioning: Product data alerts allow Google to notify you by email as soon as a problem with your eligible products is detected.
strengths: Default email when active products drop significantly (e28)
weaknesses: Only Google-side, and only large drops by default
Doesn't see the store's own stuck jobs

competitors.name: Meta Commerce Manager / Meta for WooCommerce
competitors.positioning: Manually : regularly check the Diagnostics view of your catalog.
weaknesses: Monitoring is manual or build-your-own API (e30, e31)

competitors.name: CatalogCanary
competitors.positioning: When the feed breaks — products silently vanish, required fields go missing, a run hangs and never finishes — you find out weeks later when your ad performance craters.
weaknesses: Meta only; replaces the feed rather than monitoring alongside it

competitors.name: Product Feed Manager (RexTheme) / WP Product Feed Manager
competitors.positioning: New: Add smart feed health monitoring with admin notices and email alerts for failed or incomplete feed runs.
weaknesses: Only for their own feeds; alerts paused (e39) or noisy (e54)

competitors.name: Feed Health Monitor / FeedProof / PodSync (2026 WP.org entrants)
competitors.positioning: No Feed Generation Required This plugin does not generate product feeds.
strengths: Email on new critical data errors (e34, e37)
weaknesses: Local data audits, not job or platform monitoring (e36)

competitors.name: Shopify monitors (Feed Guard, Feed Sentinel, FeedKill Watch)
competitors.positioning: Feed Guard watches your Merchant Center, explains in plain language what is wrong, and repairs the product directly inside your Shopify admin.

critic.risk: A direct twin already exists: CatalogCanary ships a stuck-run watchdog and Slack alerts, yet has under 10 installs.
Nobody pays for monitoring alone: a Shopify monitor has 0 reviews, and CatalogCanary has fewer than 10 installs.
WP.org forums, where the pain lives, ban promotion.
Feed vendors already email on failed runs (WP Product Feed Manager, RexTheme) and can improve that cheaply.
Google side becoming free: real-time approval-status push API, plus a default drop email.
Meta may already email on catalog errors (third-party source only).
Reading Meta-side status needs catalog_management App Review.
Google Merchant API requires OAuth verification.
critic.rebuttal: Google says verification typically takes 3-5 business days (e59).
Two searches found no shutdown. The pattern is entrants with no traction, not deaths (e52, e43).

win_plan.positioning: The watchdog for the sync plugin you already run: it tells you when the dashboard says "no errors" and nothing is syncing.

switching_triggers.trigger: A plugin update leaves feeds or sync frozen
switching_triggers.move: Answer the thread with the Scheduled Actions diagnosis (no links on WP.org)

offers: Agency license covering all client stores
Local-only, so no Google or Meta account access needed

build_first.feature: Pending/failed Action Scheduler watcher for gla, wc_facebook, adt_pfp and woo_feed hooks
build_first.why: pain: jobs stall quietly (e5, e6, e10)

build_first.feature: Feed file staleness and item-count drop alerts

where_to_find.why: German store owners with sync failures (e9)

trust: Reads only local data; no account tokens

pricing.recommendation: Test a $149/yr agency license (unlimited client sites), not $79 per store
pricing.competitor_range: $4.99/mo Shopify monitors to $249.50/yr agency feed tiers; Optmyzr from $209/mo
pricing.rationale: Single-store monitoring shows no buyers. Agencies already pay multi-site tiers and sell monitoring as a service (e60, e61).

validation.experiment: Offer 10 WooCommerce agencies a refundable $149/yr founding license for a local-only multi-site sync watchdog.
steps: Day 1: list 20 agencies from the Woo Slack and the Facebook group
Days 2-5: DM with the 'dashboard says no errors' story

kill_criteria: Agencies say vendor failure emails are enough
